verifications.method: Coordinate/trig: DL = BD sinB, DM = DC sinC
verifications.check_code:
import sympy as sp
# General triangle B=(0,0), C=(2,0), A=(p,q); D=(1,0). Distance from D to AB equals to AC.
p,q=sp.symbols('p q',real=True)
A=sp.Matrix([p,q]);B=sp.Matrix([0,0]);C=sp.Matrix([2,0]);D=sp.Matrix([1,0])
def dist2(P,U,V):
    cr=(V-U)[0]*(P-U)[1]-(V-U)[1]*(P-U)[0]
    return cr**2/((V-U).dot(V-U))
eq=sp.together(dist2(D,A,B)-dist2(D,A,C))
num=sp.factor(sp.numer(eq))
sols=sp.solve(num.subs(q,3),p)  # q>0 sample height
assert sols==[1]  # A lies on perpendicular bisector of BC -> AB=AC
# isosceles yes; not necessarily right/equilateral/obtuse (counterexample q=3,p=1: sides sqrt10,sqrt10,2)
AB2=(A-B).dot(A-B).subs({p:1,q:3}); AC2=(A-C).dot(A-C).subs({p:1,q:3}); BC2=4
checks={'A':AB2+AC2==BC2 or AB2+BC2==AC2 or AC2+BC2==AB2,
        'B':AB2==AC2==BC2,
        'C':max(AB2,AC2,BC2)*2>AB2+AC2+BC2,
        'D':AB2==AC2}
assert [k for k,v in checks.items() if v]==['D']
steps: DL = BD sin B, DM = DC sin C
BD = DC and DL = DM give sin B = sin C
B = C (B+C<180), so AB = AC: isosceles

from itertools import product
# region = membership in (C,R,S,T); a model = set of nonempty regions
regions=list(product([0,1],repeat=4))
regions=[r for r in regions if not (r[2] and not r[3])]  # all S are T
import itertools
def valid(m):
    return any(r[0] and r[1] for r in m) and any(r[1] and r[2] for r in m)
I=II=III=True
cnt=0
for mask in range(1,1<<len(regions)):
    m=[regions[i] for i in range(len(regions)) if mask>>i&1]
    if not valid(m): continue
    cnt+=1
    if any(r[0] and r[3] for r in m): I=False
    if not any(r[1] and r[3] for r in m): II=False
    if any(r[1] and not r[3] for r in m): III=False
res=(I,II,III)
opts={"A":(True,True,False),"B":(True,False,False),"C":(False,False,True),"D":(False,True,False)}
assert res==opts["D"]
assert all(res!=opts[k] for k in "ABC")
